events.title: Airtable spreadsheet-database launched
events.summary: Airtable launched in February 2015 — a spreadsheet interface with [relational database]s, views, and [API] access for lightweight ops and content workflows.
events.about: Airtable let non-engineers build mini-apps — kanban, calendars, and forms on top of linked tables — while developers used its REST [API] for glue scripts. Startups tracked hiring pipelines, content calendars, and bug triage without standing up Postgres; it influenced Notion databases and the no-code movement.

narrative.whyChosen: Airtable made databases approachable for PMs and ops teams without [SQL].
narrative.whyImportant: Its [API] let developers integrate spreadsheet UX with custom automation.
narrative.problemSolved: Teams hacked together Google Sheets for relational data that needed structure and permissions.

events.title: NVIDIA Jetson TK1 released
events.summary: NVIDIA announced the Jetson TK1 on March 17, 2015 — a Tegra K1 developer board for CUDA-powered edge AI and [computer vision].
events.about: Jetson brought [GPU] compute to embedded robots, drones, and [IoT] gateways — developers ran TensorFlow and OpenCV on a $192 board with 192 CUDA cores. Later Jetson Nano, Xavier, and Orin modules powered production edge ML. It paired NVIDIA's CUDA ecosystem with maker-style single-board hardware.

narrative.whyChosen: Jetson TK1 was NVIDIA's first CUDA-capable embedded developer board.
narrative.whyImportant: It made [GPU]-accelerated inference practical on edge devices outside datacenters.
narrative.problemSolved: Edge projects needed local neural-network inference without cloud latency or a full desktop [GPU].

events.title: Bazel open-sourced
events.summary: Google open-sourced Bazel on March 24, 2015 — a fast, hermetic build system derived from Google's internal Blaze tool.
events.about: Bazel builds C++, Java, [Go], and more from declarative BUILD files with aggressive caching and reproducibility — one command rebuilds only what changed. Monorepos at Google scale inspired its design; TensorFlow, Angular, and many open-source projects adopted it. Example: `bazel build //myapp:server` produces identical artifacts locally and in CI.

narrative.whyChosen: Bazel brought Google's monorepo build model to the open-source world.
narrative.whyImportant: It proved hermetic, cacheable builds could work outside Google's walls for large polyglot codebases.
narrative.problemSolved: Make, Maven, and Gradle struggled with incremental builds and dependency isolation in huge repos.
